> Is DIO1 presence a strict requirement, could it be the reason for this problem?

DIO1 is only needed for advanced features, like channel activity detection, or direct reception in FSK mode.

You're using a 20.8 kHz bandwidth. For LoRa, that's quite narrow, since your transmitter and receiver frequency need to be within +-25% bandwidth in order to receive - in your case that's +- 5.2 kHz. From my experience, the crystals on cheap LoRa modules are pretty bad, and can easily shift the RF frequency by several kHz. Try increasing bandwidth to something like 125 kHz to rule this out.

@jgromes , I was also trying with 125 with the same result, I was also trying to transmit with RadioLib and receive with arduino-LoRa library as RadioLib->arduino-LoRa and it was able to receive packets transmitted with RadioLib, but not the other way and not between RadioLib->RadioLib with transmit-receive examples. 

Just to summarize:

- RadioLib->RadioLib : does not work
- RadioLib->arduino-LoRa: works
- arduino-LoRa->arduino-LoRa: works
- arduino-LoRa->RadioLib: does not work

Unfortunately I'm unable to replicate this issue using two SX1278 modules with Arduino Uno, running RadioLib at both ends. The only problem that I did noticed was that at 20.8 kHz bandwidth, I had to manually tune transmitter frequency to get into that +-25% window.

That leads me to believe it might be a configuration mismatch between transmitter and receiver (you never posted your full sketches). Does the issue persist if you use default configuration, i.e. calling `radio.begin()` without arguments?

Also, do you have the latest master of the library (the one with the output power fix)?

@jgromes, I was setting output power to higher level during my tests. Do you have ESP32 board to test? I noticed that arduino-LoRa is using ICACHE_RAM_ATTR for ESP32 for ISR:
```
#if (ESP8266 || ESP32)
    #define ISR_PREFIX ICACHE_RAM_ATTR
#else
    #define ISR_PREFIX
#endif
```

If you don't have the `ICACHE_RAM_ATTR` attribute prior to the interrupt service routine `setFlag`, then it should lead to a crash if that function is called within interrupt context - you haven't reported that.

Repeating what I asked for in my previous comment: try with the default configuration, and post full RadioLib sketches that cause this issue.

1. Try to add the `ICACHE_RAM_ATTR` prior to `setFlag()`, i.e. `void ICACHE_RAM_ATTR setFlag(void)`.

2.  Try using the default configuration by calling `radio.begin()`.

> Are SX1278 modules fully supported on ESP32, anybody tested them on ESP32 platform?

RadioLib is platform-agnostic, all modules and protocols are supported on all platforms. There are many projects using SX127x specifically on ESP32, for example the [TinyGS project](https://tinygs.com/).

These modules, which I'm using have frequency drift no more than 1.5 kHz, I was using them extensively without any problems with 20.8, 31.25, 41.7 bandwidths with arduino-LoRa library.
Yes, after this change, it works down to BW=15.6 with frequency error of 1.4 kHz, 7.8 and 10.4 did not work before due to too large frequency difference, with another library, too.

The errata fix applies to the entire family of SX1276/77/78/79 chips, so that's not a factor.

To be honest, there have been issues with the fix in the past. Seeing as it's not required for the radio to function and only mitigates spurious receiver response (under some conditions), I'm going to place the entire errata fix behind a compile-time macro, which will be disabled by default. That way, most users don't have to worry about low-bandwidth operation, but the fix remains accessible for those that need it.
Should be fixed now by the last commit, thanks for reporting!
